fills.researcher_notes: This is one of ten rows in the gtsou-core-operator brief, all inside government-controlled Ukraine (or, for cross-border rows, their Ukrainian section). Since 1 Jan 2020 the certified transmission system operator is Gas TSO of Ukraine LLC (ТОВ «Оператор ГТС України», GTSOU), unbundled from Ukrtransgaz/Naftogaz under the Energy Community-mandated unbundling law signed 15 Nov 2019 (company founded 4 Feb 2019, took over technical operation 1 Jul 2019, certified as the independent operator 1 Jan 2020). Verified via (1) ENTSOG's own European gas-TSO membership directory, which lists "LLC Gas TSO of Ukraine" as the Ukrainian member/observer TSO, and (2) Ukrainian Wikipedia's dedicated GTSOU article, an independent source giving the exact Ukrainian legal name and the full unbundling timeline. These are two independent origins (an industry association's own directory vs. an encyclopedia article), both verified OK, so tier=high. This answer was established once for the whole brief and is applied here rather than re-derived per row. utg.ua and tsoua.com (GTSOU's own site) both 403 to url_verifier -- a WAF block, not a deletion -- so the operator's own site was not needed as primary evidence; ENTSOG + uk.wikipedia stand on their own. This does NOT extend to occupied-territory or wholly Russian-side pipe, which are out of this brief's scope. This row is the Tula-Shostka-Kiev line, cross-border Russia→Ukraine (Tula Oblast start). The GTSOU answer above covers the Ukrainian section. For the Russian section, ru.wikipedia's dedicated article on Gazprom transgaz Moscow explicitly lists "Тула — Шостка — Киев" (Tula-Shostka-Kiev) by name among the trunk lines it operates, alongside other Kiev-direction lines from the same Tula hub -- a specific, line-named match, not a generic system claim. That is one source naming this exact line, so the Gazprom transgaz Moscow half of the value is medium-strength on its own; combined with the high-tier GTSOU half for the Ukrainian section, the joint value is proposed at tier=medium overall (the weaker of the two components governs). This is NOT the escalated 'Gazprom attributed ownership of Ukrainian pipe' defect (gotcha 4) -- Gazprom transgaz Moscow is named here only for the Russian-side section of a genuinely transnational line, matching the row's own StartCountryOrArea=Russia. [Leg-3 review 2026-08-15] Independence check: the pair originally cited here was ENTSOG's member list plus a Ukrainian-language Wikipedia article, and a tertiary encyclopaedia is not a second independent ORIGIN under the project's tier rules. Added GTSOU's own 'Key facts' page (Wayback 2020-06-03, live origin 403s behind the operator WAF), which states the legal name 'Gas TSO of Ukraine LLC' outright. The high tier therefore rests on ENTSOG (third-party European TSO association) + the operator's own primary statement; the Wikipedia link is retained as a reading aid and is NOT counted toward independence.
